subject: Essential Mathematics
topic: Area of a Part of a Circle

unit.substrand: Sub-Strand2.5: Area of a Part of a Circle
unit.careers: Illustrative pattern/material-design practices;no real door/site-clearance qualification.
unit.focus: Sector/segment boundaries,minor/majorareas,actual safe paper models and bounded design/sweep applications.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional decorator removes a circular cap but subtracts a whole wedge and confuses majorsector with majorsegment.
unit.drivingQuestion: Which boundaries and measurements justify a circle-part area? KICD: Where do we use area of part of a circle in real life?
unit.storylineThread: Boundaries → sector → actualsector → minorsegment → majorcomplement → actualsegment → sweep → capapplication → audit → independent evidence.
unit.content: Area of a sector; Area of a segment
unit.coreCompetencies:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner explores different options of improvising cutouts of sectors of a circle for working out their areas.
Learning to Learn: the learner acquires new knowledge as they discuss with peers how to work out areas of circular objects.
Citizenship; learners appreciate their immediate environment as they gather locally available circular objects
unit.values:
Unity: The learner exhibits devotion and honesty by undertaking the task while working with peers to make paper cutouts of sectors of a circle and obtain the measurements.
Peace: the learner displays care and tolerance while discussing with peers and obtaining circular objects, tracing and marking out sectors and segments.
unit.pcis: Education for Sustainable Development: the learner uses locally available circular objects to trace and mark out sectors and segments, and work out the areas.

assessment.subjectLabel: AREA OF A PART OF A CIRCLE
assessment.instructions: Lesson10,40minutes:4procedure,12sections1–2,16sections3–4,4silentcheck,4collection. Work independently with CP10only,blankpaper and calculatorπ/degree mode. No teaching cards,peers,hints or media. Show labelled boundaries/formulas/units;retain exactπexpressions and round final nonexact areas to2decimalplaces.

sections.title: 1. Sector boundary and area
sections.prompt: Draw FinalAsector with centre,radii,arc and centralangle labelled. Compute its area. Explain why the arc-length formula would have the wrong units for this question.

sections.title: 2. Minor segment partition
sections.prompt: For FinalBdraw the minor sector,chord and centraltriangle. Compute sector,triangle and minorsegment areas;explain the subtraction and one rounding/measurement limit.

sections.title: 3. Major segment and a useful sweep
sections.prompt: Find FinalBmajorsegment by complement and show the two segment areas sum to the whole circle. Distinguish majorsegment from majorsector. Draw and compute FinalCpaper-door-sweep area,and state a condition/limitation for its use.

sections.title: 4. Application and actual model evidence
sections.prompt: Explain one useful application of sector/segment area and one limit involving boundary choice,fit,waste or actual measurement. Describe one actual individual observation needed before claiming you made/measured a cut-out. Explain why exact fictional data alone do not establish that action.
